correctness.rationale: The full source formula (1.4) reduces to exact c_j updates with h=floor((5t-1)/m). For fixed n=5q+r, all block limits are affine in q and all summands degree <=2, giving coefficients polynomial degree <=3 in q. Sixteen exact rational identities at q=0,1,2,3 prove the four formulas for every nonnegative q. The rational Bernstein expansion on eight subintervals shows all 384 relevant coefficients strictly positive, while the q^3/q^2 factor (x+2)(4x^2+2x-1)^2 is nonnegative. Hence s^-5 Q(s)>0 on the unit circle. Reciprocity and c_0>0 yield five roots strictly inside; published kernel denominator does not vanish on the associated interior slice. Files verify_hartogs.py and BERNSTEIN_CERTIFICATE.json are exact and rerunnable.

originality.rationale: The 2025/2026 full primary source explicitly calls difference five open in Section 4.3, while proving only differences 1, 2 and reporting 3, 4, 6. The new result proves the whole infinite, coprime difference-five family and its exact five-root count; earlier generic zero existence and selected fixed-difference families do not imply this. The 2016/2017 primary source covers all parameters gamma>=2 but explicitly leaves (1,2) unresolved. Searches for parameter aliases and stronger formulations returned no decisive covering theorem; unindexed and forthcoming source results remain risks.
residual_risks: An unpublished work in preparation by the source authors is explicitly mentioned; it may contain a solution not yet public.
An unindexed proof of the same degree-ten positivity statement could exist. Search noncoverage is not a proof of global novelty.
The 2017 primary comparison focused on its explicit zero theorem and introductory scope; not every technical appendix was independently rederived.

value.rationale: Section 4.3 of the primary paper specifically isolates k=5 as more difficult because phi(5)=4, while k=3,4,6 were settled. Proving the infinite remaining family for all four residue classes is a motivated conjecture subcase, not isolated finite computation. The constructed positive phase and rational Bernstein certificate establish a structural inequality for canonical Bergman numerator polynomials and transfer to genuine kernel zeros.
